We use the tools of applied microeconomics to study how South African households
make financial decisions, and which policies would make consumer financial
markets work more efficiently and more equitably. We seek out and use relevant
survey and administrative data from sources in the public and private sectors.

## Research themes

Our work is organised into themes. Each output below is tagged with the theme it
belongs to; use the tags to filter the list.

**Mortgage pricing in South Africa.** Using a unique dataset of mortgage
applications, we study how banks price home loans in South Africa, how this
pricing varies with borrower characteristics, and how willing households are to
switch lenders.

**The market for funeral insurance.** Funeral insurance is one of the most widely
purchased financial products in South Africa; life insurance remains far less
common. Yet the two products deliver very similar benefits to households — cash
in the event of a death — at different prices. Our work on this theme explores
the drivers of demand for these products, the extent to which they are
substitutes, and the implications for household welfare and public policy.
